newsitem.title: FRANCE: French officials deny sleaze amnesty plans.
newsitem.headline: French officials deny sleaze amnesty plans.

text.p: Aides to French Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Tuesday denied a report that he planned an amnesty of political sleaze if his centre-right majority retains power in a snap parliamentary election.
The report in the satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine said Juppe had told key allies one of his priorities after the May 25-June 1 election would be to push through an amnesty law.
Officials at Juppe's office described the report as "election campaign slander."

The usually well-informed weekly said Juppe had told leaders of the centre-right UDF, a junior coalition partner, that he planned an amnesty law "in one form or another" and a law on reform of the offence of misappropriation of company funds.
The offence is at the heart of a wave of corruption investigations targeting dozens of company managers.
In 1990, a parliament dominated by the left voted an amnesty law for party political funding offences which sparked furious controversy.

Le Canard quoted Juppe as telling former defence minister Francois Leotard and education minister Francois Bayrou that he was ready to take responsibility for such a law because, according to him, all political parties were implicated in funding probes.
"I will explain (to public opinion) that the biggest French companies are losing their market share abroad because of investigations underway," the Canard Enchaine quoted Juppe as saying.

The weekly added that a new National Assembly elected for five years would vote for an amnesty law "because the deputies will know that they have five months ahead of them to make people forget about it".
